t:
(a) In General.—Section 1902(a) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (81), by striking “and” at the end; 
        (2) in paragraph (82), by striking the period at the end and inserting “; and”; and 
        (3) by inserting after paragraph (82) the following new paragraph:“(83) provide that, not later than January 1, 2017, in the case of a State plan (or waiver of the plan) that provides medical assistance on a fee-for-service basis or through a primary care case-management system described in section 1915(b)(1) (other than a primary care case management entity (as defined by the Secretary)), the State shall publish (and update on at least an annual basis) on the public website of the State agency administering the State plan, a directory of the physicians described in subsection (mm) and, at State option, other providers described in such subsection that—“(A) includes—“(i) with respect to each such physician or provider—“(I) the name of the physician or provider;“(II) the specialty of the physician or provider;“(III) the address at which the physician or provider provides services; and“(IV) the telephone number of the physician or provider; and“(ii) with respect to any such physician or provider participating in such a primary care case-management system, information regarding—“(I) whether the physician or provider is accepting as new patients individuals who receive medical assistance under this title; and“(II) the physician’s or provider’s cultural and linguistic capabilities, including the languages spoken by the physician or provider or by the 
skilled medical interpreter providing interpretation services at the physician’s or provider’s office; and“(B) may include, at State option, with respect to each such physician or provider—“(i) the Internet website of such physician or provider; or“(ii) whether the physician or provider is accepting as new patients individuals who receive medical assistance under this title.”.  
    (b) Directory Physician or Provider Described.—Section 1902 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396a), as amended by section 5005(a)(3), is further amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(mm) Directory Physician or Provider Described.—A physician or provider described in this subsection is—“(1) in the case of a physician or provider of a provider type for which the State agency, as a condition on receiving payment for items and services furnished by the physician or provider to individuals eligible to receive medical assistance under the State plan, requires the enrollment of the physician or provider with the State agency, a physician or a provider that—“(A) is enrolled with the agency as of the date on which the directory is published or updated (as applicable) under subsection (a)(83); and“(B) received payment under the State plan in the 12-month period preceding such date; and“(2) in the case of a physician or provider of a provider type for which the State agency does not require such enrollment, a physician or provider that received payment under the State plan (or a waiver of the plan) in the 12-month period preceding the date on which the directory is published or updated (as applicable) under subsection (a)(83).”. 
    (c) Rule of Construction.—
        (1) In general.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall not be construed to apply in the case of a State (as defined for purposes of title XIX of the Social Security Act) in which all the individuals enrolled in the State plan under such title (or under a waiver of such plan), other than individuals described in paragraph (2), are enrolled with a medicaid managed care organization (as defined in section 1903(m)(1)(A) of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1396b(m)(1)(A))), including prepaid inpatient health plans and prepaid ambulatory health plans (as defined by the Secretary of Health and Human Services). 
        (2) Individuals described.—An individual described in this paragraph is an individual who is an Indian (as defined in section 4 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act (25 U.S.C. 1603)) or an Alaska Native.  
    (d) Exception for State Legislation.—In the case of a State plan under title XIX of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396 et seq.), which the Secretary of Health and Human Services determines requires State legislation in order for the respective plan to meet one or more additional requirements imposed by amendments made by this section, the respective plan shall not be regarded as failing to comply with the requirements of such title 
solely on the basis of its failure to meet such an additional requirement before the first day of the first calendar quarter beginning after the close of the first regular session of the State legislature that begins after the date of enactment of this Act. For purposes of the previous sentence, in the case of a State that has a 2-year legislative session, each year of the session shall be considered to be a separate regular session of the State legislature.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that state involvement, a public website, and providers "participating" in a case-management system amount to participation. But the section only imposes a Medicaid state-plan requirement that states publish a provider directory, which is disclosure of information to the public, not outside input into a federal decision. Phrases like "as defined by the Secretary" and the Secretary's determination about State legislation are unilateral federal actions with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: the State shall publish (and update on at least an annual basis) on the public website of the State agency administering the State plan, a directory of the physicians described in subsection (mm)

qwen_block.w: This section requires State agencies to publish a directory of physicians on their public websites. While this makes information available to the public, it does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The definition of participation requires the federal government to consult with outsiders; here, the obligation is on the State to provide information, and there is no mechanism for public input into federal decision-making. The mention of 'public website' refers to the location of the directory, not a public comment period or hearing.
qwen_block.s: the State shall publish (and update on at least an annual basis) on the public website of the State agency administering the State plan, a directory of the physicians described in subsection (mm)

opus.w: The section requires States to publish a Medicaid provider directory. That is a duty to give information to beneficiaries, not a process where outside parties are consulted before a federal decision. The closest candidates don't qualify: 'as defined by the Secretary' does not expressly call for rulemaking, and the Secretary decides alone whether State legislation is needed. The word 'participating' only refers to providers enrolled in a State program, not to anyone taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: the State shall publish (and update on at least an annual basis) on the public website of the State agency administering the State plan, a directory of the physicians described in subsection (mm)
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section talks about States publishing a directory on a public website, uses the word "participating" for providers in a case-management system, mentions terms "as defined by the Secretary," and lets the Secretary decide whether State legislation is needed. That could look like participation. It isn't, when checked against the definition:
   - **The directory:** The State publishes it for Medicaid beneficiaries. It gives people information. It does not bring anyone outside the government into a federal decision.
   - **"Participating":** Here it describes providers enrolled in a State program, not a process for weighing in on a decision.
   - **"As defined by the Secretary":** This lets the Secretary define a term. Unlike Example 6, it doesn't expressly say the Secretary acts "by regulation," so no rulemaking is required.
   - **State legislation:** The Secretary decides this alone, with no consultation, hearing, or comment period.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates that States publish a directory of physicians on their public websites. This is a transparency or disclosure requirement, not a participation mechanism. The definition of participation requires consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties before a federal decision is made. Publishing a list does not involve the federal government consulting with the public or providers to make a decision; it merely provides information to them. Therefore, it does not meet the criteria for participation.
qwen_chat.s: the State shall publish (and update on at least an annual basis) on the public website of the State agency administering the State plan, a directory of the physicians described in subsection (mm)
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring States to publish a directory of physicians on a public website constitutes "participation" because it involves the general public accessing information. However, the definition of participation requires that the federal government consult or coordinate with outside parties *before* making a decision, or that outside parties have a role in the decision-making process (e.g., advisory boards, comment periods). Here, the State is simply mandated to disclose information; there is no requirement for the federal government to consult with the public or the providers before making a regulatory or funding decision. The action is unilateral disclosure, not collaborative decision-making.
